In 7-dimensional [[geometry]], there are 127 [[uniform 7-polytope|uniform polytopes]] with E<sub>7</sub> symmetry. The three simplest forms are the [[3_21 polytope|3<sub>21</sub>]], [[2_31 polytope|2<sub>31</sub>]], and [[1_32 polytope|1<sub>32</sub>]] polytopes, composed of 56, 126, and 576 [[vertex (geometry)|vertices]] respectively.

They can be visualized as symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s in [[Coxeter plane]]s of the E<sub>7</sub> Coxeter group, and other subgroups.

== Graphs ==
Symmetric [[orthographic projection]]s of these 127 polytopes can be made in the E<sub>7</sub>, E<sub>6</sub>, D<sub>6</sub>, D<sub>5</sub>, D<sub>4</sub>, D<sub>3</sub>, A<sub>6</sub>, A<sub>5</sub>, A<sub>4</sub>, A<sub>3</sub>, A<sub>2</sub> [[Coxeter plane]]s. A<sub>k</sub> has ''k+1'' symmetry, D<sub>k</sub> has ''2(k-1)'' symmetry, and E<sub>6</sub> and E<sub>7</sub>  have ''12'', ''18'' symmetry respectively.

For 10 of 127 polytopes (7 single rings, and 3 truncations), they are shown in these 8 symmetry planes, with vertices and edges drawn, and vertices colored by the number of overlapping vertices in each projective position in progressive order: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta, red-violet.
